HUBB should remain in the reference lane: it is a credible scaled competitor in power utility hardware but exposure is diluted by broader Utility Solutions and Electrical Solutions businesses.

PWR and MYRG are not hardware suppliers but are useful demand-side validation anchors. Their transmission project backlog, materials management commentary, and procurement constraints may lead or confirm order growth at hardware suppliers.

Need another pass focused on private competitors and distribution channels: MacLean Power Systems, S&C Electric, Southwire, AFL, utility distributors, OPGW/ADSS suppliers, galvanized tower/fastener suppliers, and certification/testing labs may explain bottleneck severity but may not be directly investable.

HUBB should be retained as a reference leader rather than an underfollowed pure play; its transmission hardware catalog is relevant, but exposure is diluted inside a larger electrical-products company.

ACA and VMI are adjacent infrastructure suppliers rather than fittings pure-plays; later layers should test whether transmission structures are a parallel procurement bottleneck linked to the same utility qualification and construction-cycle constraints.

MYRG is not a hardware supplier but may serve as a demand/procurement timing proxy for hardware suppliers because it performs transmission and distribution construction work.

node: Transmission-line hardware, fittings, conductor accessories, and installation-enabling components
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the universe around the transmission-line hardware/fittings node using a two-lane Serenity funnel. The cleanest underfollowed direct exposure is Preformed Line Products, a small-cap manufacturer of products used in transmission, distribution, communications, and utility asset inspection. Hubbell is the obvious diversified reference competitor with power utility line-construction hardware but less pure exposure. Quanta Services and MYR Group are included as direct customer/installation-demand anchors rather than hardware manufacturers, because hardware procurement and qualified product availability should precede or enable their transmission construction work. Layer 1B expanded the investable universe for transmission-line hardware and installation-enabling components. The clearest underfollowed candidate is Preformed Line Products, which appears unusually close to the node through formed-wire, conductor-support, splice, termination, substation connector, OPGW, and fiber hardware exposure. Hubbell is the main public reference peer for transmission components but has diluted exposure inside a much larger electrical-products platform. Arcosa and Valmont are not fittings pure-plays, but they are adjacent scarce infrastructure suppliers through engineered transmission, distribution, and substation structures. The key research question for later layers is whether hardware procurement, utility qualification, and line-installation productivity create earlier-cycle order signals than EPC revenue recognition.
